import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Read the data
data = pd.read_csv(pd.io.common.StringIO("""brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR"""))

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Price vs Megapixels with size representing weight
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
scatter = ax1.scatter(data['megapixels'], data['price_usd'], 
                     s=data['weight_grams']/3, alpha=0.6, 
                     c=data['model_year'], cmap='viridis', edgecolors='black', linewidth=1)
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_title('Price vs Megapixels\n(size=weight, color=year)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax1, label='Year')

# 2. Brand distribution
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
brand_counts = data['brand'].value_counts()
colors = plt.cm.Set3(range(len(brand_counts)))
ax2.bar(brand_counts.index, brand_counts.values, color=colors, edgecolor='black', linewidth=1)
ax2.set_xlabel('Brand', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_title('Camera Count by Brand', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 3. Sensor type distribution pie chart
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
sensor_counts = data['sensor_type'].value_counts()
ax3.pie(sensor_counts.values, labels=sensor_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%',
        startangle=90, colors=plt.cm.Pastel1(range(len(sensor_counts))))
ax3.set_title('Sensor Type Distribution', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')

# 4. Weight vs Price
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
for brand in data['brand'].unique():
    brand_data = data[data['brand'] == brand]
    ax4.scatter(brand_data['weight_grams'], brand_data['price_usd'], 
               label=brand, s=100, alpha=0.7, edgecolors='black', linewidth=1)
ax4.set_xlabel('Weight (grams)', fontsize=10)
ax4.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax4.set_title('Weight vs Price by Brand', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(fontsize=8)
ax4.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 5. Max ISO by brand
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
brands = data['brand']
iso_values = data['max_iso']
colors_map = plt.cm.tab10(np.linspace(0, 1, len(data)))
bars = ax5.barh(range(len(data)), iso_values, color=colors_map, edgecolor='black', linewidth=1)
ax5.set_yticks(range(len(data)))
ax5.set_yticklabels([f"{brands.iloc[i]}" for i in range(len(data))], fontsize=9)
ax5.set_xlabel('Max ISO', fontsize=10)
ax5.set_title('Max ISO by Camera', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax5.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3)

# 6. Model year timeline
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
ax6.scatter(data['model_year'], data['price_usd'], s=data['megapixels']*5,
           c=data.index, cmap='coolwarm', alpha=0.6, edgecolors='black', linewidth=1)
ax6.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=10)
ax6.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax6.set_title('Price Timeline\n(size=megapixels)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax6.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 7. Body type distribution
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
body_counts = data['body_type'].value_counts()
ax7.bar(body_counts.index, body_counts.values, color=plt.cm.Set2(range(len(body_counts))),
       edgecolor='black', linewidth=1)
ax7.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=10)
ax7.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=10)
ax7.set_title('Body Type Distribution', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')

# 8. 4K Video capability
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
video_4k_labels = ['No 4K', '4K']
video_4k_counts = [len(data[data['has_video_4k'] == 0]), len(data[data['has_video_4k'] == 1])]
colors_4k = ['#ff9999', '#66b3ff']
ax8.pie(video_4k_counts, labels=video_4k_labels, autopct='%1.1f%%',
       startangle=90, colors=colors_4k, explode=(0.05, 0.05))
ax8.set_title('4K Video Capability', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')

# 9. Summary statistics table
ax9 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
ax9.axis('off')
stats_text = f"""Camera Dataset Summary
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Total Cameras: {len(data)}
Brands: {data['brand'].nunique()}

Avg Price: ${data['price_usd'].mean():.2f}
Avg Megapixels: {data['megapixels'].mean():.1f}
Avg Weight: {data['weight_grams'].mean():.0f}g

Year Range: {data['model_year'].min()}-{data['model_year'].max()}
4K Support: {(data['has_video_4k'].sum()/len(data)*100):.0f}%"""

ax9.text(0.1, 0.5, stats_text, fontsize=10, verticalalignment='center',
        family='monospace', bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='wheat', alpha=0.3))

plt.suptitle('Camera Dataset Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
